summary: On 2026-11-24 the average stock rose 0.22% and 66% of stocks rose, so the 74.2% hit rate is only 8 points above always-UP (66.0%). Stock selection looked real: UP calls beat the market 70% of the time, and the UP-minus-DOWN spread was +4.7 pp. The model leaned UP on 89% of calls. Realised moves (2.2%) were about four times the expected moves (0.58%). The costliest misses were mostly UP calls on semiconductor, AI-hardware and power-equipment stocks, which fell 5-11%, while the best DOWN calls were on stocks that had jumped 10-20% the day before. Web search found no reliable same-day recap, so the cause of the tech drop is unconfirmed. Market pulse on the next morning shows extreme fear (VIX 30.8) and QQQ -3.8%, which suggests the tech weakness continued.
went_well: The give-back rule on stocks that jumped 9-20% the day before picked the biggest DOWN winners (ADI, HPE, DELL, TXN, MU), and UP calls beat the market 70% of the time.
went_wrong:
Many UP calls rested on 'futures slightly higher, extreme fear backdrop', which has no stock-level information; the 35 IT stocks called on give-back or oversold logic averaged -6.4%. It was knowable that the sector had run hard the day before, but a single day is not enough to call it a rule.
Expected move sizes (0.58%) were far below the realised 2.2%, so confidence and size are poorly calibrated.

summary: On 2026-11-25 the average stock rose 0.59% and 69% of stocks rose, so always-UP scored 68.6% while our calls scored 33.6%. The index close was mixed (S&P 500 -0.25%, Nasdaq -0.62%, Dow +0.33%) after a violent intraday selloff (Nasdaq low about -4.6%) that reversed by the close; breadth and the equal-weighted stock universe finished up. The morning forecast saw weak futures and VIX 26 and called 94% of stocks DOWN, so the market direction call was wrong. Stock selection was roughly neutral: UP calls beat the market 46.5% of the time and the UP-minus-DOWN spread was -0.03 pp, so the miss was almost all the lean, not skill. Yesterday the lean was 89% UP (hit 74%, only 8 points above always-UP), so the lean swung from one extreme to the other on a single macro signal.
went_well: DOWN calls on semiconductor and AI names (ASML, LRCX, ORCL, MU) did fall 4.5-5.8%, so sector-level tech-weakness reading had some value; Health Care rel_hit 65%.
went_wrong:
Lean 6% UP vs 69% actually up: every call carried the same 'futures/asia weak, vix 26' rationale, so a single market-level signal set the direction of nearly all 574 stocks. Knowable: the lean itself is controllable before the open; the intraday reversal was not.
The costliest misses (HPQ +11.5%, CHTR +8.4%, AXON +7.4%, CDW, ADI, TXN, EXE) were DOWN calls on stocks that rallied in a broad rebound; no stock-specific news was found, so they are market-driven, not noise worth stock-level rules. Stock-specific cause for each was not confirmed by search.

research_focus: Check the actual US close and the pre-market futures for the previous session rather than intraday extremes, and say whether a selloff reversed. After two days of extreme fear (VIX above 26, fear and greed 15) look for rebound evidence: breadth, small caps, oversold counts. Look for stock-specific news (earnings, guidance, analyst moves) on stocks being called DOWN.
summary: On 2026-11-26 the average European stock rose 1.85% and 94% of stocks rose, so always-UP scored 94.4% while our 71 calls scored 53.5%. The lean was balanced (51% UP, the cap-market-lean rule worked mechanically), but the market was a broad rebound: UP calls were right 97% (n=36) and DOWN calls only 9% (n=35). Stock selection was mildly positive: UP calls beat the market 64.8% of the time, spread +0.47 pp, and the best calls were oversold bounces in banks, cyclicals and defence. The costliest misses were DOWN calls justified by exposure to a US tech selloff after the European close; the US index close on 11-25 was nearly flat (SPY +0.23%, QQQ -0.24%, IWM +1.2%) after an intraday reversal, so the carry-over fear was priced out. Realised moves (1.9%) were nearly three times the expected moves (0.68%). Web search returned no same-day recap, so causes beyond the broad rebound are unconfirmed.
went_well:
Oversold-bounce UP calls (SAN.MC, RHM.DE, ABBN.SW, BBVA.MC) gained 2.7-4.1%; UP calls were right 97% and beat the market 64.8% of the time.
The market lean was balanced at 51% UP, so there was no repeat of the one-signal extreme lean of 11-24 and 11-25.
went_wrong:
35 DOWN calls were right only 9% of the time; many were justified by exposure to an after-close US tech selloff that had already partly reversed by the US close. This was knowable: the pre-open brief could have checked the US close and futures rather than the intraday low.
Many DOWN calls at confidence 0.51-0.53 carried a 'no edge' rationale (rose yesterday, give-back likely); with 94% of stocks up, they added only noise.
Expected move sizes (0.68%) were far below the realised 1.92%, a repeat of the size underestimate seen on earlier days.

summary: On 2026-11-27 (Black Friday half-day) the average stock rose 1.33% and 81% of stocks rose, so always-UP scored 81.0% while our 574 calls scored 69.3%. The S&P 500 closed +1.60%, the Nasdaq +2.31% and the semiconductor index about +4.7% as AI-profitability fears faded after a rough month, a broad risk-on rebound. The lean was 78% UP, close to the market's 81%, so the shortfall came from DOWN calls (about 129 calls on overbought/mean-reversion or weak-trend rationales, right only about 24%) on a day when everything rebounded. Stock selection was slightly negative on relative terms (UP calls beat the market 44.8%, spread +0.22 pp), so 69% is mostly the market and not skill; the best calls were beaten-down memory/optical AI names (SNDK, COHR, MU) that rebounded hard. Realised moves (1.54%) matched expected moves (1.42%) this time. The costliest misses (GNRC, IP, SW, HONA, AXON, INTC, TXN, ADI) were cyclicals, paper/packaging and chip names that rose 4-7% with no company-specific news found, apart from GNRC data-center power momentum; they were beta moves in a market-wide short squeeze and not knowable at the open beyond the futures signal.
went_well: UP calls on oversold/rebound or positive-futures rationales were right 82-96% (n=445), and the lean of 78% UP was near the actual 81%, avoiding the 11-25 style swing.
went_wrong:
DOWN calls justified by 'extended/overbought, mean-reversion' or 'weak trend, rebound likely to fade' were right only 25% and 22% (n=71 and n=58) on a day when futures were up and the market rebounded; these were pure technical fades with no stock-specific negative news, so the market-wide rebound was partly knowable from futures.
The 30-70% lean cap in cap-market-lean was not honoured (78% UP), although the breach did no harm today because the market rose 81%.
